subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the real part of (z + 1)/(z + i) is 1, find the locus of z.

mark_split.label: Write the quotient in terms of x and y
Multiply by the conjugate and separate real and imaginary parts
Set the real part to 1 and state the locus

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the locus — what you substitute for z, what you multiply by, and what you set the real part equal to.
insider_note: A locus answer must end as an equation in x and y — here the squares cancel and the line x − y = 1 is that equation. The imaginary part of the numerator is never used, so writing it out in full costs time and earns no mark.

steps.label: Substitute z = x + iy
steps.margin_note: First mark. The +1 on top joins x; the +i below joins iy. Write each of numerator and denominator as (real) + i(imaginary).
steps.memory_tip: The +1 on top joins x; the +i below joins iy. Write each line as (real) + i(imaginary).

recall.must_convey: That z = x + iy is substituted so the quotient becomes [(x + 1) + iy] over [x + i(y + 1)].
accept: put z equals x plus i y so the top is x plus one plus i y and the bottom is x plus i times y plus one
substitute x plus i y and group the real and imaginary parts above and below
the fraction becomes x plus one plus i y over x plus i y plus one

steps.why: The locus is an equation in x and y, so z must be replaced first. The grouping fixes the form of the conjugate: the denominator's imaginary part is (y + 1), not y.
common_mistakes: Grouping the +i in the denominator with x.
Writing the numerator as x + 1 + y, dropping the i.

steps.label: Multiply by the conjugate
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The conjugate of the denominator is x − i(y + 1). The denominator becomes x² + (y + 1)²; the real part of the numerator is x(x + 1) + y(y + 1).
steps.memory_tip: The conjugate of x + i(y + 1) is x − i(y + 1). The numerator's imaginary part is never used.
lines: Multiply above and below by x − i(y + 1):

recall.must_convey: That multiplying by the conjugate x − i(y + 1) makes the denominator x² + (y + 1)² and gives real part (x² + y² + x + y) over it.
accept: multiply by the conjugate x minus i times y plus one, the denominator is x squared plus y plus one squared and the real part on top is x squared plus y squared plus x plus y
rationalise the denominator and separate the real part x squared plus y squared plus x plus y
after the conjugate the real part of the numerator is x squared plus y squared plus x plus y
conjugate tho multiply chesi real part x square plus y square plus x plus y teeyali
make the denominator real with the conjugate and collect the real terms
heard_as: x minus i y plus one

steps.why: The real part of a quotient can be read only when the denominator is real. The conjugate does that in one multiplication; the denominator x² + (y + 1)² is then the thing that cancels against the numerator in the last step.
common_mistakes: Using x + i(y + 1) instead of x − i(y + 1).
Expanding the imaginary part in full — it is never used.

steps.label: Real part = 1
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Set the real part to 1, cross-multiply, and the squares cancel — the locus is a straight line.
steps.memory_tip: Real part = 1 here, not 0. Both x² and y² cancel, so the locus is the line x − y = 1, with z ≠ −i.
lines: ⇒ x² + y² + x + y = x² + y² + 2y + 1

lines.text: ∴ Locus of z: x − y = 1, z ≠ −i

recall.must_convey: That setting the real part equal to 1 and cancelling the squared terms leaves x − y = 1 as the locus.
accept: put the real part equal to one, the x squared and y squared cancel and the locus is x minus y equals one
cross multiply, the squares cancel, x minus y equals one
real part one gives x plus y equals two y plus one so x minus y is one
real part one pettithe squares cancel ayyi x minus y equals one vasthundi
the locus is the straight line x minus y equals one

steps.why: The condition 'real part is 1' is used exactly here. Because the denominator x² + (y + 1)² also has x² + y² in it, both squares cancel and only a linear equation survives — the locus is a line, not a circle. One point must be removed: at z = −i the denominator z + i is zero, so the expression is undefined there. That point is (0, −1), and 0 − (−1) = 1 — it lies on the line, so it has to be excluded by name or the stated locus contains a point that is not in it.
common_mistakes: Setting the real part to 0, which is the 'purely imaginary' condition, instead of to 1 as asked.
Leaving z = −i in the locus, where the expression is undefined.
